Nvidia’s sales grew 78% on AI demand and the company gave strong guidance, CNBC reported [[n0354]]. The stock still fell, and Nvidia was downgraded by Summit Insights Group amid AI-market concerns [[n2583]].
EPS Upside Watch

The set-up is in the equipment and foundry names the chip-deal and Intel stories touch. Nvidia and Broadcom testing chips on Intel’s manufacturing process [[n2584]] makes Intel the wildcard, and Intel closed at 22.74 USD, up 17.04% over 20 sessions.
⚡ Breaking Convention
Intel is up 17.04% over 20 sessions while the chip ETF is down 7.78%. The market is paying for the foundry story while the designers are being sold, the reverse of the usual AI-designer leadership.

earnings_pattern.title: Raised outlooks are paid, soft guides are sold
parts: Rewarded

A raised outlook paid in the last two weeks. Rolls-Royce upgraded its forecasts and its shares soared more than 18% [[n5214]]. EMCOR headed toward its best single-day gain in a year on an upbeat Q4 and a strong outlook [[n5091]], and Honest Company rose after Q4 revenue topped estimates [[n5100]]. Snowflake posted a big beat and the stock jumped [[n0355]]. Super Micro surged once it filed its delayed 10-K [[n5044]], and Hut 8 surged on a profit boom even though its Q4 revenue missed [[n2627]].
Punished

A soft guide or a quality question was sold. Hims & Hers plunged 22% on concerns over the weight-loss business and margins [[n5019]]. Pure Storage fell 12% in premarket trade despite a Q4 beat [[n5207]], and Rocket Lab slipped despite a Q4 sales surprise [[n5209]]. Nvidia’s optimistic forecast failed to convince Wall Street [[n0358]], and the stock fell 9% on tariff fears [[n2585]]. Ready Capital shares plunged 28% after a Q4 loss and a dividend cut [[n2593]].
Pattern

The market pays for the next-quarter number, not for the beat. Revenue beats with raised outlooks were rewarded, with EMCOR, Honest and Rolls-Royce as the examples [[n5091]] [[n5100]] [[n5214]]. Beats that did not lift the stock were sold, with Pure Storage, Rocket Lab and Nvidia as the examples [[n5207]] [[n5209]] [[n0354]] [[n2585]]. The EPS figure matters less than the guide that follows it.
Attention into EPS

Vail Resorts is the pending release in the group, per Yahoo Finance’s earnings preview [[n0375]], and JD.com’s Q4 preview calls its report pivotal amid growth opportunities and profitability challenges [[n0370]]. JD closed at 40.24 USD, down 3.96% in the prior session and 1.18% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03). CoreWeave filed for its IPO [[n2525]], and Reuters reported its revenue surge in the US filing [[n3295]], so the filing is the next big disclosure in the AI-cloud group.
Playbook

Buy names where the guide is being raised and the stock has lagged, and sell rallies in names that beat with a soft outlook. Into JD’s print, own the stock only on a pullback below its 40.24 USD close rather than on the preview. The call changes if a guidance cut arrives from one of the sector leaders, because that would confirm the breaking-convention read in semis.

underowned.title: Uranium and the reactor fuel chain
parts: Attention Gap

Reactor developers get the headlines. Reuters reported Siemens Energy supplying Rolls-Royce with equipment for small nuclear reactors [[n5275]], and CNBC reported Palisades signing an agreement to build small modular reactors in Michigan [[n5035]]. Fuel is quieter. The uranium ETF URA closed at 23.49 USD, down 17.03% over 20 sessions, and Cameco at 41.11 USD is down 16.85% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03).
Exposure & Risk

URA, Cameco and Centrus Energy, which closed at 84.00 USD and is up 2.07% over 20 sessions, are the instruments. The risk is that fuel producers are price-takers in a policy-driven build-out, and a reactor delay hits them with a lag. A sharp fall in URA can outrun any change in the fundamentals.
Trigger to Watch

A fuel or enrichment contract from one of the reactor developers named above would move the theme from the reactor story to the fuel story. URA reclaiming its 28.31 USD reference from 31 January would confirm the rebound.

underowned.title: Copper miners as a grid and AI-capex metal
parts: Attention Gap

The metal is doing the talking, not the miners. Copper closed at 4.58 USD per pound, up 7.38% over 20 sessions, while the copper-miners ETF COPX is down 1.13% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03). European attention is building around mining: Money.pl argued that Europe must invest in its mining sector [[n4876]].
Exposure & Risk

COPX and Freeport-McMoRan, at 35.53 USD, are the instruments. Copper is an asset here, not a China gauge, so China demand is not the thesis. Operational shocks are the miner-specific risk, and Business Insider Polska reported a series of strong tremors at two KGHM mines [[n4826]].
Trigger to Watch
COPX reclaiming its 38.18 USD reference from 31 January, or copper holding above its 4.26 USD reference from the same date, would make the miners a consensus trade.

underowned.title: Gold miners lagging the metal
parts: Attention Gap

Gold gets the consumer headlines. Mining.com reported Americans buying gold [[n5237]], and Reuters reported India’s gold demand improving as prices retreat from an all-time high [[n5238]]. The miners lag the metal: GDX closed at 39.71 USD, up 1.93% over 20 sessions, while gold futures closed at 2,901.10 USD, up 3.15% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03).
Exposure & Risk

GDX and Newmont, at 42.36 USD and down 0.84% over 20 sessions, are the instruments. Miners carry operating and cost risk that the metal does not, so if gold stalls, the miners fall harder than the metal.
Trigger to Watch
GDX holding above 39.71 USD while gold holds above its 2,812.50 USD level from 31 January would confirm that the miners are catching up with the metal.

underowned.title: Japanese domestic equities through EWJ
parts: Attention Gap

The Nikkei is a headline story but a quiet ETF story. Nikkei Asia reported trading-house stocks rallying as Buffett hinted at more buying [[n4198]], and The Japan Times wrote that Japanese stocks have stalled at 1989 levels [[n2569]]. The country ETF EWJ closed at 69.21 USD, up 1.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03).
Exposure & Risk

EWJ and the Nikkei are the instruments. The risks are a stronger yen, with USD/JPY down 2.96% over 20 sessions, and tariffs on Japanese exporters. A firm yen compresses the export margins that the domestic-demand story has to replace.
Trigger to Watch

Wage talks are the domestic-demand trigger: The Japan Times reported metalworker unions demanding a record pay hike [[n4256]]. A settlement that holds the pay gains would strengthen the domestic leg; EWJ holding 69.21 USD with USD/JPY near 150.7710 would confirm it.

crypto.title: The reserve rally has unwound
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 86,065.67 USD, down 8.68% in the prior session and 10.11% over 20 sessions, after CNBC reported it tumbling 9% and reversing most of the rally from the Trump reserve announcement [[n1625]] (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-03). Ether fell 14.85% in the prior session to 2,145.57 USD and is down 17.57% over 20 sessions. Solana fell 20.43% to 142.02 USD and is down 28.27% over 20 sessions, while XRP fell 18.77% to 2.39 USD in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-03). The equity wrappers carry the leverage to the move. Coinbase closed at 205.75 USD, down 29.38% over 20 sessions, Strategy at 250.92 USD, down 25.05%, and the spot bitcoin ETF IBIT at 48.90 USD, down 15.27% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03).
New / Most Important

The reserve trade is the story, and it is coming apart. Reuters reported Trump naming cryptocurrencies in a strategic reserve and sending prices up [[n1679]]. CoinDesk reported that one trader made millions betting $200 million on bitcoin just before the reserve news [[n1658]]. Fortune reported that XRP and Solana soared and then faltered once the multi-asset reserve plan was announced [[n1692]]. Open interest in bitcoin futures fell to a six-month low [[n1619]], and TradingView reported a record $2.9 billion of outflows from crypto funds [[n1661]].
Playbook

Stay underweight crypto beta into the reversal. Do not add to the coins the reserve named until they reclaim their pre-announcement levels, and treat bitcoin’s 95,747.43 USD close from 11 February as the level that would change the call. CoinDesk put bitcoin above $84K on 1 March [[n1576]], so that is the near support. A close below $80,000 would confirm the reserve bid has failed, as Decrypt reported the slide toward that level on 28 February [[n1513]]. Own the spot ETF only on a close back above the 57.71 USD level from 31 January, which would show the flows returning.

flows.title: Liquidity tightens at the edges while buybacks hold
parts: Global Liquidity

Liquidity is tightening at the margin. Bloomberg reported credit spreads on their longest widening streak since 2023 [[n3261]]. The ECB’s stance is split: a Reuters Morning Bid column says the bank may stumble into stimulus [[n2910]], and a separate Reuters piece asks five questions about the tougher calls ahead [[n2943]]. The policy signal is therefore not one-directional. The longer-run warning came from Ray Dalio, who said a debt crisis could cause an “economic heart attack” for the US economy within three years [[n8646]]. Central-bank balance sheets are not the marginal driver right now; the marginal driver is tariffs and the rate path, and that will be the story the market trades on.
Rates & Dollar

The Treasury curve is bull flattening. The 10Y closed at 4.16% and is down 42 bps over 20 observations, and the 2Y at 3.96% is down 26 bps over the same window (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-03). TLT, the 20-plus-year Treasury ETF, rose 5.48% over 20 sessions to 92.57 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03). The dollar is the second leg: the US Dollar Index is at 106.75 index points, down 1.49% over 20 sessions, and FXStreet reported the dollar tanking near 1% as European geopolitics and Trump’s tariffs undercut it [[n2948]]. Traders placed a record bet on the yen [[n4350]], which is the same dollar-weakness trade seen from Tokyo.
Credit Check

Credit is the check engine, and it is flashing. Spreads are widening for the longest streak since 2023 [[n3261]], and the high-yield ETF HYG closed at 79.59 USD, down 0.16% over 20 sessions, while the investment-grade ETF LQD, at 109.54 USD, rose 1.94% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03). The quality premium is widening. Bloomberg reported that bosses are talking about distress at the lowest level since before Lehman collapsed [[n2774]], a mixed signal against the spread data that argues corporate balance sheets are better than the bond market implies. Ready Capital’s dividend cut is a reminder that credit stress reaches small lenders first [[n2593]], and private credit is spreading into new markets, with AFR reporting global private credit funds set to storm Australia [[n5184]].
Equity & Fund Flows

Buybacks are the flow holding up. Dell raised its dividend 18% and launched a $10 billion buyback [[n3264]], and Trip.com announced a $400 million buyback as its stock fell 12% [[n3318]]. Options flows surged instead of fund flows: Cboe reported zero-day options reaching a 56% share of SPX options in February [[n5387]]. Reuters reported hedge funds ramping up bets on falling stocks [[n3170]], and the crypto complex saw its record $2.9 billion outflow [[n1661]]. Buybacks are the corporate bid, while the hedge book and the options desk are leaning the other way. Business Insider reported that the gap between hedge fund haves and have-nots is wider than ever [[n3313]], which suggests the crowding is concentrated in a few large books rather than spread across the industry.
Portfolio Implication

Hold more duration than equity beta. The long end of the Treasury curve works while the curve keeps flattening from the bull side, so keep TLT as the hedge rather than the core. Own the buyback names on a stabilising tape, with Dell at 95.56 USD, down 7.76% over 20 sessions, as the test. Stay underweight HYG against LQD while spreads keep widening. The call turns constructive on credit if spreads narrow for two straight sessions, and a fresh record in crypto outflows would confirm the risk-off read.

anticipatory.title: Tariff start on Tuesday
parts: What Is Priced

The market is pricing the 25% tariffs as a launch date rather than a bluff. Reuters reported the Canada and Mexico levies locked in to launch on Tuesday, and stocks tumbled [[n3926]]. AP quoted Trump saying there is “no room” for delay [[n3928]]. The Canadian dollar and the Mexican peso hit one-month lows as the tariffs were set to take effect [[n3257]]. The S&P 500 is already down 3.16% over 20 sessions and the VIX is at 22.78 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03).
Conditional Expression

If the tariffs take effect and China’s counter-tariffs of up to 15% start on March 10 [[n1259]], the trade is long volatility and short cyclicals. Buy VIX exposure sized small, and reduce the materials and industrials ETFs into strength, with XLB down 2.04% and XLI down 2.86% over 20 sessions. If the tariffs are delayed, the VIX should fall back toward its 16.43 level from 31 January, and the rally would favour the cyclicals.
Risk

The risk is a whipsaw. The start date can move, and the S&P 500 has already lost 3.16% over 20 sessions, so a delay would produce a sharp relief rally. Size any hedge to survive that reversal rather than to catch the exact top.

anticipatory.title: Ukraine truce versus the defence bid
parts: What Is Priced

Defence stocks are pricing a longer conflict with more European spending. The London summit set out a peace plan, and The Guardian summarised Starmer’s takeaways [[n3782]]. Macron floated a one-month Ukraine truce [[n3886]], and Reuters reported the White House seeking a plan for possible Russia sanctions relief [[n3828]]. Rheinmetall, at 1,144.50 EUR, is up 49.80% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03).
Conditional Expression

If a truce firms, sell into the defence rally: trim Rheinmetall and the German defence names, and buy the broad STOXX 600 instead. If the talks fail, the defence bid extends and the euro-area growth bid fades. The trade is asymmetric because the defence move is already large, so the downside from a truce is faster than the upside from a breakdown.
Risk

The truce is a headline risk rather than a signed outcome. The Guardian wrote that Europe has a lot to do before it can exert real influence on a Ukraine peace deal [[n3832]], so the proposal can move the defence names on words alone and reverse as quickly.

anticipatory.title: The US jobs print and the bond rally
parts: What Is Priced

Growth worry is priced into the jobs data. Reuters’ week-ahead said investor angst about the economy will be tested by the US jobs data [[n0366]], and jobless claims jumped to 242,000 in the latest week [[n8192]]. The 10Y is at 4.16% and is 42 bps lower over 20 observations, so the rate market is already pricing softer data (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-03).
Conditional Expression

A weak print extends the bull flattening: buy the long Treasury through TLT, which is up 5.48% over 20 sessions, and keep equity beta light. A firm print reverses it: sell the long end and accept a steeper curve, while the Nasdaq 100, down 4.90% over 20 sessions, has room to fall further only if yields rise.
Risk

The risk is that a weak print is read as recession rather than as a rate cut. That combination lifts the VIX and drags credit spreads wider, which is the scenario in which the bond rally stops protecting the equity book.

anticipatory.title: ECB decision and the euro
parts: What Is Priced

The euro-area rate path is the second decision. Reuters’ Morning Bid says the ECB may stumble into stimulus [[n2910]], and Reuters asks five questions about the tougher calls ahead [[n2943]]. EUR/USD closed at 1.0414, up 1.62% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03), so the market has not yet bought the euro-area weakness.
Conditional Expression

If the ECB signals more easing, sell the euro and hold the Euro Stoxx 50, which closed at 5,540.69 and is up 6.19% over 20 sessions. If it sounds firm, euro strength hurts the export-heavy DAX, which rose 8.02% over 20 sessions, so reduce the index exposure into that move.
Risk

Plumbing is the side risk. The ECB’s multi-trillion-euro payment system had an outage in late February [[n2843]], a reminder that operational events can move the market’s view of the central bank even when policy is unchanged.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — chip-export overhang

Nvidia fell 9% on tariff fears [[n2585]] and was downgraded by Summit Insights amid AI-market concerns [[n2583]]. Buy puts or a put spread struck below 114.06 USD for a rally-failure play. Invalidation is a close above 120.07 USD with the chip ETF SOXX reclaiming its 218.13 USD level from 31 January.

Buy TSM once the announcement confirms the deal, and hedge with SOXX puts, since the chip ETF is down 7.78% over 20 sessions. Invalidation is a close below 172.97 USD after the announcement.

catalysts.title: $DELL — the buyback opens the window
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Dell boosted its dividend 18% and launched a $10 billion buyback [[n3264]], after a full-year EPS beat [[n0364]]. Capital return on that scale is a support mechanism, and it arrives while the stock is under pressure.

Buy shares or a call spread around 95.56 USD. Invalidation is a close below 95.56 USD that the buyback fails to defend, which would signal the hardware cycle is the bigger force.

Buy on pullbacks toward the 162.02 USD close, and invalidate on a close below that level, which would show the analyst call has failed to hold the stock.

parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Hims & Hers plunged 22% on concerns over the weight-loss business and margins [[n5019]], and Reuters reported looming curbs on drug compounding clouding the forecast [[n5020]]. The regulatory overhang is the catalyst, and it has not gone away.

Sell rallies into the 40.68 USD level or buy puts for the regulatory overhang. Invalidation is a clear delay to the compounding curbs, which would remove the catalyst.

catalysts.title: $JD — the pivotal print

A Moomoo preview calls JD’s Q4 report pivotal, with growth opportunities set against profitability challenges [[n0370]]. The print is the next catalyst, and the question is whether the profitability trade-off is working.
Price Hurdle & Risk
The hurdle is the 40.24 USD level, and the risk is that the stock trades with the China consumer complex rather than on its own print.
Trade Expression

Stay neutral until the print. Buy only if the profitability question clears, and hedge the China consumer exposure with KWEB, since the names trade together on the same policy headlines. Size any position so that a profitability miss does not dominate the book.

spec.retail_intro: The dominant popular-narrative trade is the same-session crash bet, in which zero-day options let the crowd buy protection against tariffs, a mechanism that any run of heavy call buying shares: the crowd’s option buying forces dealers to hedge, and the hedging becomes the move.

retail.title: Zero-day options / VIX — betting on the crash by the close
parts: Why Retail Is Here

A crash bet is easy to sell when it does not have to wait a month to pay. Zero-day options expire within the session, so a trader can buy protection after the tariff headlines and be finished by the close. Bloomberg reported zero-day trading hitting a record on Trump’s turmoil and a Robinhood push [[n5412]], and Livewire Markets described options traders betting on a stock-market crash, spooked by tariffs and US recession risk [[n5378]]. The scoreboard is the VIX, which closed at 22.78 on 3 March (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03). Traders tend to watch the 16.43 level from 31 January: a fall back to it would mean the protection has been paid for and is losing value.
What Is Driving It

The VIX rose 16.05% in the prior session and is up 38.65% over 20 sessions from 16.43, a move of 6.35 points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03). The stock market is moving with it. The S&P 500 fell 1.76% on 3 March and is down 3.16% over 20 sessions to 5,849.72 from 6,040.53 on 31 January, the Nasdaq 100 is down 4.90% over 20 sessions, and the three-times Nasdaq ETF TQQQ is down 15.28% over 20 sessions to 70.08 USD. The catalyst is trade policy. Reuters reported Trump locking in tariffs on Canada and Mexico to launch on Tuesday, with stocks tumbling [[n3926]], and AP News quoted Trump saying 25% tariffs on Mexican and Canadian imports would start Tuesday, with ‘no room’ for delay [[n3928]]. The bond market leans the same way: the 10-year yield is 4.16%, down 42 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-03), and the dollar index is down 1.49% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03).
The Social Signal

The attention is in the options flow and in the language around it. Cboe Global Markets reported SPX zero-day options jumping to a record 56% share in February [[n5387]]. MarketWatch wrote that options traders are bracing for a stock-market crash [[n5377]], and Hedgeye had already charted 0DTE SPX option volume at the end of February [[n5171]], so the flow is building rather than arriving overnight. The brokerage piece matters most. A Robinhood push puts the product in front of retail accounts, which makes the flow the crowd’s own behaviour rather than a commentator’s view of it [[n5412]].
Historical Analog

The closest analog is a mechanism rather than a dated episode, and it runs in two waves. First come the early call buyers: their options force the dealers who sold them to buy stock as a hedge, and that hedging pushes the price higher. Second comes the crowd, which buys the same options after the move is already visible, so the squeeze depends on late buyers continuing to arrive. A crash bet runs the same loop in reverse. Dealers who sold puts sell stock as the market falls, and the crowd buys protection after the first leg down. Retail is in the second wave for the same reason: the contract is easy to buy after a visible drop, while the first wave of hedgers is already positioned.
Smart Money View

The institutional view is split on pace more than on direction. Hedgeweek reported that hedge funds boosted bearish stock bets amid rising volatility [[n3279]], and Reuters reported hedge funds ramping up bets on falling stocks at the end of February [[n3170]]. Steve Cohen’s turn to negative on DOGE and tariffs, with a ‘significant correction’ possibly coming, is the bear case in its plainest form [[n2973]]. The bull case is quieter and stock-specific. Ark Invest bought the dip in Tempus AI as Cathie Wood snapped up shares [[n5077]], and Morgan Stanley’s Lisa Shalett called the retreat in Big Tech an ‘idiosyncratic’ stock-picking moment [[n5116]]. Hedge funds are adding bearish stock bets while Ark buys single names, so the argument is about how far the market falls, not whether the best companies are cheap.
When the Narrative Breaks

The trade breaks on three observable triggers. The first is the tariff date: AP News reported the 25% tariffs were set to start Tuesday [[n3928]], and Fortune described Wall Street holding its breath to see whether Trump enforces them or pulls back at the last minute [[n0377]]. A pullback takes the premium out of the crash bet, and a zero-day option decays to nothing by the close if the market does not move. The second is the VIX: a fall back toward its 16.43 reference from 31 January would mean the crash bet is paying less, and a close above 25 would say the crowd is winning. The third is the index. The S&P 500 at 5,849.72 needs to reclaim 6,040.53, and TQQQ at 70.08 is 15.28% below its 82.72 reference from 31 January (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03). The instrument risk is time and leverage: a zero-day option has one session to work, and a three-times ETF can move several times the index in a day.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — the top pick is back
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The pitch is that Wall Street has given it permission. Morgan Stanley sees Tesla reaching $430 and has reinstated it as its top pick over the AI and robotics play [[n5369]], and Elon Musk predicts Tesla’s profit could grow tenfold over the next five years [[n2556]]. Tesla closed at 284.65 on 3 March, down 29.65% over 20 sessions from 404.60 on 31 January (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03), so a top pick arriving after the drop reads as a bargain. Electrek reported on 3 March that Tesla’s chairwoman sold $33 million of TSLA, framing it as letting Musk ‘destroy the brand’ [[n7169]], and Berkshire Hathaway’s $1.07 trillion market value passed Tesla’s [[n2540]]. A sale framed as brand damage tends to be read as political rather than as a verdict on profits.
Where It Breaks

The breakpoint is the sales base. Business Insider reported Tesla’s sales almost halved in Europe and were surpassed by a Chinese rival [[n5657]], and Bloomberg reported Koreans who plowed into leveraged ETFs were burned by a 40% plunge in Tesla [[n5222]]. The instrument risk is leverage: the three-times Nasdaq ETF TQQQ is down 15.28% over the same 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03), so a leveraged way into the dip can lose more than the stock. A close below 250 would tell the crowd the Morgan Stanley call is not holding the price.

retail.title: Solana / SOL — the reserve rally that faltered
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story is still Washington’s reserve, which reads as a government buyer. Trump named Solana and XRP among the coins for a strategic reserve [[n1601]], and Axios called the result a $300 billion global crypto rally sparked by Truth Social posts [[n1602]]. On 3 March the rally reversed. Fortune’s headline was that XRP and Solana soared and then faltered [[n1692]], and AP News called the move a short-lived surge [[n1681]]. Solana closed at 142.02 USD, down 20.43% in the session and 28.27% over 20 sessions from 197.98 on 11 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03).
Where It Breaks

The 197.98 close from 11 February is the reference traders tend to anchor on, and $140 is the round line the price is testing now; a close below it turns the reserve bid into liquidation. Bitcoin is the test for the whole complex. CNBC reported it tumbling 9% and reversing most of the rally from the announcement [[n1625]], and it closed at 86,065.67 USD, down 10.11% over 20 sessions from 95,747.43 on 11 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03). The flow is the warning: a record $2.9 billion left crypto funds [[n1661]]. The instrument risk is timing: one trader made millions betting $200 million on bitcoin just before the reserve news [[n1658]], and buyers who arrive after the headline carry the reverse risk.

retail.title: NuScale / SMR — the AI power fever moves to gas
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The pitch is that AI needs more power than the grid can supply, and small modular reactors are the clean way to supply it. Palisades’ agreement to build the first of its kind small modular reactors in Michigan made the case [[n5035]], and Reuters reported Siemens Energy supplying equipment for Rolls-Royce’s small reactors [[n5275]]. The trade has a skeptic, though. Seeking Alpha’s note on NuScale is titled ‘Sell’, arguing that small modular reactors are unestablished and costly [[n5031]]. NuScale closed at 15.45 USD, down 10.12% in the session and 35.19% over 20 sessions from 23.84 on 31 January (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03).
Where It Breaks

The break is the rotation. WSJ reported on 1 March that AI fever in power stocks had moved from nuclear to plain natural gas [[n6680]], and Jim Cramer said he was ‘very, very skeptical’ of nuclear power trades [[n6190]]. NuScale published its fourth-quarter and full-year results on 3 March [[n2582]], and the stock fell 16.31% over five sessions, so the market is waiting for proof that the reactor case pays. Oklo and Nano Nuclear are down 29.39% and 29.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-03), so the group moves together, and a 10% session shows how little cushion a single name has.
